Permissioned audited access to unmasked originals and configurable masking rules
acceptance: Only roles granted explicit permission (DataSoft Administrator by default) can view original unmasked text; everyone else, including other tenants, sees masked text (404 for other banks).
Every original-content view appends an audit event (actor, request, timestamp) to the hash-chained audit log.
Administrator can add/disable masking patterns via API; detection uses active patterns; built-in patterns cannot be weakened below OTP/card defaults.
Text extracted from text-type attachments is masked before any NLP processing.
Tests: two banks, unauthorized users, audit append, custom pattern applied.

tasks.title: Precomputed embeddings, semantic labels, vector topic clustering and evaluation
acceptance: Embeddings (multilingual-e5-small, local files only) are computed once from MASKED text with E5 prefixes (passage: for stored requests, query: for drafts) when a request is submitted/edited, via the transactional outbox or an idempotent job; never on the search read path. Store model id, preprocessing version and dimension with each vector; vectors from a different model/version are never compared. A management command backfills missing embeddings.

Similar-request retrieval: within the authenticated tenant only, exact (no HNSW/IVF index) pgvector cosine top-40 + lexical top-40 (Postgres simple FTS ts_rank_cd and pg_trgm similarity, enabled by migration) fused with RRF k=60; return at most 5 above a configurable minimum-relevance gate. Lexical-only fallback when ML is offline or vectors missing; submission never depends on ML.
Each suggestion includes deterministic match evidence: shared key terms/phrases between the draft and the candidate (no LLM).

Label suggestions: tenant-specific weighted kNN over embeddings of that bank's accepted labelled requests, with cap on near-duplicate examples; cold-start labels use the embedded label description as a prototype (lower-confidence, flagged tentative); per tenant x label thresholds with abstention; feedback records accepted, rejected and corrected suggestions. No centroids, examples or caches shared across banks.

Topic proposals: per tenant, agglomerative clustering (cosine, average linkage, configurable distance cutoff default 0.3) over stored vectors of recent unlabelled requests (default 90 days), clusters of size >= 3 only, skipped when fewer than 20 eligible requests; titles from cluster c-TF-IDF terms plus representative request snippets shown to admin. Use scikit-learn/numpy/scipy only if already locked for the package; no new dependencies.

Evaluation harness: management command over a synthetic English/Bangla/Banglish fixture with graded relevance (2 duplicate, 1 related, 0 unrelated) including hard negatives (same module, different problem); reports HitRate@5, Recall@5, nDCG@5, MRR@5 for lexical vs dense vs hybrid, broken down by language variant, and writes an experiment manifest (model id/revision, prefix scheme, fusion settings, dataset split, metrics). Tests use a deterministic fake embedder and assert hybrid >= lexical on the fixture.
Tests: two banks (no cross-tenant results, labels or clusters), ML offline fallback, masking before embedding, no embedding writes during search, version mismatch ignored.

tasks.title: Banglish normalization and embedding model comparison harness
acceptance: Deterministic Banglish normalization (versioned): Unicode NFC, whitespace/punctuation cleanup, protected technical tokens (OTP, RTGS, BEFTN, NPSB, error codes like E105, module names) never altered, and a reviewed domain dictionary in a data file mapping common romanized Bangla spelling variants (e.g. ashche/ashe/ashtese, hocche/hoche, partesi/parchi, na) to canonical Bangla forms. Original masked text is always kept; the normalized view is added as a supplemental lexical/embedding input, never replacing user text. No new dependencies (no IndicXlit).
Normalization runs after masking and before lexical indexing/embedding; bump preprocessing version so stale vectors are ignored and backfill can re-embed.

Model comparison: the evaluation command accepts configurations (embedder path/id, prefix scheme symmetric vs asymmetric, normalization on/off, fusion) and runs a matrix: lexical, dense, hybrid, hybrid+normalization, and any alternative local checkpoints present under ML_MODELS_DIR (e.g. gte-multilingual-base, a Banglish E5 checkpoint); missing checkpoints are skipped with a clear message, never downloaded. Report per language variant (English, Bangla, Banglish, code-switched, typo) and p50/p95 embedding latency, and write the experiment manifest.

Expand the synthetic fixture with Banglish variants, typos and hard negatives (same error code, different failure); split by underlying incident before augmentation so no near-clones leak between splits.

Tests: normalization preserves protected tokens and is idempotent; normalization improves or does not hurt lexical HitRate@5 on the Banglish fixture with a fake embedder; two-bank isolation unaffected; matrix runner skips missing models.

tasks.title: Comments on workflow actions and attachment quarantine
acceptance: Every workflow action (submit, accept, reject, assign, deliver, verify pass/fail, close, reopen) accepts an optional comment stored with the history event and shown per visibility rules.
Uploaded attachments start QUARANTINED; a pluggable local scanner (default: signature/EICAR + type/size check, no paid service) marks CLEAN or REJECTED; only CLEAN files can be downloaded.
UI shows comment field on actions and attachment scan status.
Tests including EICAR rejection and cross-tenant download denial.

tasks.title: Attachment quarantine fixes: legacy backfill, non-UTF-8 safety, every-action comment tests
acceptance: A data migration rescans existing attachments still marked with the legacy unscanned status, using the same local scanner, and sets them to CLEAN or REJECTED, so previously valid files stay downloadable. The migration is reversible as a no-op.
Text attachments that are not valid UTF-8 never cause a 500: decode with errors=replace or skip text masking, and the upload is atomic (no attachment row left behind if processing fails).
REJECTED attachments are hidden from attachment listings for client users other than the uploader, and their stored file content is deleted once marked REJECTED; the metadata row stays for audit.

NEW test file(s) only: a parametrized test that every workflow action (submit, accept, reject, assign, deliver, verify pass, verify fail, close, reopen) accepts an optional comment and stores it masked with the history event; a 423 download test for QUARANTINED/REJECTED; a non-UTF-8 upload test; a legacy-backfill migration test; cross-tenant download denial still holds.
